heroLead: New Florence sits along the Conemaugh River in the far northeastern corner of Westmoreland County, a quieter part of the county's Marcellus and Utica story.
intro: This part of Westmoreland County hasn't seen the same density of drilling as areas closer to Pittsburgh, but operators have leased and developed acreage along the Conemaugh corridor over the years, and Utica shale interest deeper still has kept some tracts in play even when Marcellus activity slowed. If your family holds an interest here, it's worth a specific look rather than a general assumption based on more active neighboring counties.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around New Florence directly. We'll research your title and check on actual activity in your specific unit before making an offer.

sections.heading: A Quieter Corner of the Play
paragraphs: New Florence sits farther from the densest Marcellus development in Washington and Greene counties, which means some tracts here have been leased but not yet drilled, or drilled once with limited follow-up activity. That's a different situation than a heavily developed unit, and it changes how we approach evaluation.
Deeper Utica shale potential has drawn renewed operator interest to parts of this county over the years, so it's worth checking whether your lease covers that formation separately from the Marcellus.

sections.heading: Confirming What's Actually Happening on Your Parcel
paragraphs: We check current activity status for your specific parcel, whether that's an active producing well, a held lease awaiting development, or an expired agreement, through Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds records and operator filings.
We'll tell you plainly which situation applies to your interest rather than assuming activity that isn't actually there.

sections.heading: What a Leased-but-Undeveloped Interest Is Worth
paragraphs: Value differs meaningfully between a producing interest and one that's leased but not yet drilled. We'll walk you through how we think about each situation honestly before discussing a number.

faqs.question: My lease near New Florence has never been drilled. Do you still buy that?
faqs.answer: We evaluate leased but undrilled interests based on the operator, remaining lease term, and nearby activity, and we'll be honest if we think waiting makes more sense.

faqs.question: Does the deeper Utica shale change my interest's value?
faqs.answer: It can, if your lease covers that formation and there's operator interest in it. We check this specifically as part of our review.

faqs.question: What if my old lease has expired without ever being drilled?
faqs.answer: An expired, undeveloped lease generally returns full rights to you as the mineral owner. We'll confirm the lease status and explain what that means for your interest.
